card.summary_ko: 데릴사위로 들어와 삼 년 넘게 품삯 없이 일하는 ‘나’가 ‘키가 안 자랐다’며 성례를 미루는 장인과 벌이는 해학 가득한 실랑이.
card.summary_en: A good-humoured tale of a live-in son-in-law-to-be who has worked over three years without pay while his father-in-law keeps postponing the wedding on the excuse that the bride has not grown tall enough.

notes.ko:
**저자** 김유정(1908–1937)은 강원도 춘천 실레마을 출신으로, 지주 집안에서 태어났으나 일찍 집안이 기울었습니다. 연희전문에 들어갔다가 학업을 이어 가지 못했고, 고향에서 농민 야학을 열어 농촌 계몽에 힘썼습니다. 1935년 〈소낙비〉(조선일보)와 〈노다지〉(중앙일보)가 신춘문예에 당선되어 등단했고, 구인회에 가입했습니다. 정치적으로는 특정 조직에 속하지 않았고 카프 같은 계급문학 단체와도 거리가 있었지만, 농촌 사람들의 가난을 해학적으로 그려 사회 현실을 비추었다고 평가됩니다. 폐결핵과 가난 속에서 활동하다 1937년 3월 29세에 세상을 떠났습니다. 친일인명사전(2009)에는 수록되지 않았습니다. 〈봄·봄〉은 데릴사위 제도를 둘러싼 농촌의 풍속을 해학으로 그린 작품입니다.

**시대적 맥락** 1930년대 일제강점기 조선 농촌에서는 소작 제도와 빚으로 농민의 생활이 어려웠고, 혼인에서는 일을 시키며 사위를 들이는 데릴사위 관습이 남아 있었습니다. 〈봄·봄〉은 1935년 《조광》에 발표된 것으로 알려져 있으며, 성례를 미루며 머슴처럼 부리는 장인과 순박한 데릴사위 '나'의 갈등을 토속적 입말로 그립니다. 웃음 속에 농촌의 착취 구조를 드러낸다는 평가를 받고, 오래도록 교과서와 영화·연극으로 알려졌습니다.

**배경**
김유정(1908–1937)이 1935년에 발표한 단편으로 알려져 있다. 강원도 산골 농촌을 배경으로, 딸을 시집보내는 대신 사위를 먼저 집에 들여 일을 시키던 ‘데릴사위’ 관습을 소재로 삼았다. 일부 비평가는 이를 단순한 해학만이 아니라 노동력 착취의 풍자로도 읽는다. 「동백꽃」처럼 점순이라는 이름의 처녀가 나오지만 별개의 작품이다.

**줄거리**
‘나’는 점순이와 혼인하기를 바라며 장인(봉필)의 집에서 돈 한 푼 받지 않고 3년 7개월을 일해 왔다. 그러나 장인은 번번이 ‘점순이 키가 덜 자랐다’는 핑계로 성례를 미룬다. 점순이가 “성례시켜 달라지 뭘 어떡해” 하고 쏘아붙이자 ‘나’는 모내기 중에 배가 아프다며 드러눕고, 장인에게 뺨을 맞은 뒤 사경을 내라며 구장에게 판단을 받으러 가자고 끈다. 구장은 처음엔 성례를 시켜 주라고 하다가, 장인이 거절하자 말을 얼버무리고 뒤로 ‘나’를 따로 달랜다. 일을 팽개치면 징역을 갈 수 있다고 겁을 주기도 한다. 이튿날 아침 점순이가 “구장님한테 갔다 그냥 온담” 하며 나무라자, ‘나’는 다시 드러누워 장인과 몸싸움을 벌인다. 장인이 매질한 뒤 올 가을엔 성례를 시켜 주겠다고 달래 주고, ‘나’는 일터로 나갔다가 다시 장인을 붙들고 늘어진다. 그때 뛰어나온 점순이는 뜻밖에 ‘나’의 귀를 잡아당기며 아버지 편을 들고, 장인이 다시 매질하는 장면에서 글이 끝난다. 이 판은 작품 전문을 싣는다.

**의의**
입말과 반복되는 과장, 순박한 화자의 어리숙함이 낳는 웃음, 그 뒤에 숨은 농촌 인신 구속의 현실이 특징이다. 「동백꽃」과 함께 김유정의 대표작으로 읽힌다.

**읽기 도움**
- 데릴사위: 장차 사위가 될 사람이 처가에서 일하며 지내는 혼인 관습.
- 성례: 혼인식을 올림.
- 장인님·빙모님: 아내의 아버지·어머니. 빙모는 장모의 높임말.
- 꼬바기: ‘꼬박’의 방언.
- 짜장: 과연, 정말로.
- 애최: ‘애초’의 방언.
- 구장: 마을 일을 보던 우두머리.
- 붙배기 키: 키는 작고 옆으로 퍼진 체격을 가리키는 말.
- 모판: 볍씨를 뿌려 모를 기르는 논바닥.
- 지게막대기: 지게를 받쳐 세우는 막대기.
- 애헴: 헛기침 소리.
- 이자식·고놈: 낮추어 부르는 말투.
notes.en:
**About the author** Kim Yu-jeong (1908–1937) was from Sille village in Chuncheon, Gangwon, born into a landlord family that soon declined. He entered Yonhui College but could not continue his studies, and in his hometown he ran a night school for peasants and worked for rural enlightenment. In 1935 his stories 'Sonakbi' (Chosun Ilbo) and 'Nodaji' (Jungang Ilbo) won the new-year literary contests and he made his debut; he then joined the Gubuinhoe group. Politically he belonged to no organisation and kept apart from class-literature groups such as KAPF, but is regarded as having reflected social reality by depicting rural poverty with humour. He worked while suffering from tuberculosis and poverty and died in March 1937, aged 29. He is not listed in the 2009 Dictionary of Pro-Japanese Collaborators (친일인명사전). 'Bom-bom' humorously depicts rural custom around the live-in son-in-law system.

**Historical context** In 1930s colonial Korea the lives of farmers were hard under tenancy and debt, and in marriage the custom survived of taking in a son-in-law who worked for his bride's family. 'Bom-bom' is known to have been published in Jogwang in 1935, and in earthy spoken language it portrays the conflict between a father-in-law who puts off the wedding while working the groom like a farmhand and the simple live-in son-in-law who narrates. It is credited with exposing the exploitation of the countryside through laughter, and has long been known through textbooks, films and plays.

**Background**
This short story is generally dated to 1935 and is by Kim Yu-jeong (1908-1937). Set in a Gangwon mountain village, it draws on the custom of the live-in "deril-sawi", a future son-in-law who works at the bride's family home before the wedding. Some critics read it as satire on exploitation of labour, not only as comedy. A girl named Jeom-sun also appears in "Dongbaek-kkot", but they are separate works.

**Synopsis**
The narrator has worked three years and seven months at his father-in-law's (Bong-pil's) house without any pay, hoping to marry Jeom-sun. Each time he raises the wedding, the old man replies that she has not grown tall enough. After Jeom-sun snaps at him, "Just ask them to hold the wedding, what else?", he feigns a stomach-ache in the middle of rice-seedling work, is slapped by his father-in-law, then demands his back wages and drags him to the village headman (gujang) for judgement. The headman first tells the old man to hold the wedding, then, when he refuses, fudges and afterwards privately talks the narrator round, scaring him with talk of a jail term for abandoning the work. Next morning Jeom-sun scolds him for coming back from the headman with nothing; he lies down again and ends up grappling with the old man. After a beating, the father-in-law soothes him with a promise of a wedding this autumn and sends him back to work, but the narrator again seizes him. Jeom-sun, rushing out, unexpectedly pulls the narrator's ears and sides with her father, and the text ends as the father-in-law resumes beating him. This edition contains the whole story.

**Significance**
Its marks are spoken idiom, comic exaggeration, the laughter arising from a naive narrator, and, behind it, the reality of bound farm labour. It is read together with "Dongbaek-kkot" as Kim's best-known work.

**Reading help**
- deril-sawi: the live-in future son-in-law marriage custom.
- seongnye: holding the wedding.
- jang-in-nim / bing-mo-nim: father-in-law / mother-in-law (bingmo is honorific).
- kkobagi: dialect for "straight through, without a break".
- jjajang: really, indeed.
- aechoe: dialect for "at the start".
- gujang: the head of a village.
- butbaegi ki: a short, stocky build.
- mopan: the paddy bed where rice seedlings are raised.
- jigemakdaegi: the stick that props up an A-frame carrier.
- aehem: a throat-clearing sound.
- ija-sik / go-nom: contemptuous forms of address.

paragraphs.orig: ## 1. 자라지 않는 점순이
paragraphs.en: 1. The Girl Who Won't Grow

paragraphs.orig: “장인님! 인제 저…….”
paragraphs.en: "Father-in-law! Now, um..."

paragraphs.orig: 내가 이렇게 뒤통수를 긁고, 나이가 찼으니 성례를 시켜줘야 하지 않겠느냐고 하면 대답이 늘,
paragraphs.en: Whenever I scratch the back of my head like this and ask whether, now that I'm of age, he shouldn't let us hold the wedding, his answer is always,

paragraphs.orig: “이 자식아! 성례구 뭐구 미처 자라야지!”하고 만다.
paragraphs.en: "You rascal! Wedding, my foot! She has to grow first!" and that's the end of it.

paragraphs.orig: 이 자라야 한다는 것은 내가 아니라 내 아내가 될 점순이의 키 말이다.
paragraphs.en: This "growing" he talks about isn't about me, it's about the height of Jeom-sun, who's going to be my wife.

paragraphs.orig: 내가 여기에 와서 돈 한 푼 안 받고 일하기를 삼 년 하고 꼬바기 일곱 달 동안을 했다. 그런데도 미처 못 자랐다니까 이 키는 언제야 자라는 겐지 짜장 영문 모른다. 일을 좀 더 잘해야 한다든지, 혹은 밥을 많이 먹는다고 노상 걱정이니까 좀 덜 먹어야 한다든지 하면 나도 얼마든지 할 말이 많다. 허지만 점순이가 아직 어리니까 더 자라야 한다는 여기에는 어째 볼 수 없이 고만 빙빙하고 만다.
paragraphs.en: I came here and worked three years and a clear seven months without taking a penny. And still she hasn't grown, so I honestly can't tell when that height of hers is going to grow. If he said I should work harder, or, since he's always fretting that I eat too much, that I should eat less, I'd have plenty to say back. But when it's that Jeom-sun is still young and has to grow more, I can do nothing about it, and I just go round and round in circles.

paragraphs.orig: 이래서 나는 애최 계약이 잘못된 걸 알았다. 이태면 이태, 삼 년이면 삼 년, 기한을 딱 작정하고 일을 해야 원 할 것이다. 덮어놓고 딸이 자라는 대로 성례를 시켜 주마, 했으니 누가 늘 지키고 섰는 것도 아니고, 그 키가 언제 자라는지 알 수 있는가. 그리고 난 사람의 키가 무럭무럭 자라는 줄만 알았지 붙배기 키에 모로만 벌어지는 몸도 있는 것을 누가 알았으랴. 때가 되면 장인님이 어련하랴 싶어서 군소리 없이 꾸벅꾸벅 일만 해왔다. 그럼 말이다. 장인님이 제가 다 알아채서, “어참, 너 일 많이 했다. 고만 장가 들어라.” 하고 살림도 내주고 해야 나도 좋을 것이 아니냐. 시치미를 딱 떼고 도리어 그런 소리가 나올까 봐서 지레 펄펄 뛰고 이 야단이다. 명색이 좋아 데릴사위지 일하기에 싱겁기도 할뿐더러 이건 참 아무것도 아니다.
paragraphs.en: That's how I came to see that the contract was wrong from the very start. You ought to settle the term exactly, two years or three years, and work for that. He said just "I'll hold the wedding as the girl grows," but it's not as if anyone stands guard over her all the time, so how can anybody know when that height will grow? And I only ever knew that people's heights shoot up, who would have guessed there are bodies that stay short and only spread sideways? I thought that when the time came my father-in-law would surely see to it, so I just kept my head down and worked without a word. Now then, wouldn't it be good for me too if my father-in-law noticed it all by himself and said, "Well, you've done a lot of work. Enough, go and marry," and set us up with a household? Instead he puts on a straight face and jumps up and down in advance for fear of hearing anything of the kind, what a fuss. Live-in son-in-law is a fine name for it, but not only is the work dull, it's really nothing at all.

paragraphs.orig: 숙맥이 그걸 모르고 점순이의 키 자라기만 까맣게 기다리지 않았나.
paragraphs.en: Like a fool I didn't know that, and was waiting blindly for Jeom-sun's height to grow.

paragraphs.orig: 언젠가는 하도 갑갑해서 자를 가지고 덤벼들어서 그 키를 한번 재볼까 했다. 마는 우리는 장인님이 내외를 해야 한다고 해서 마주 서 이야기도 한마디 하는 법 없다. 우물길에서 언제나 마주칠 적이면 겨우 눈어림으로 재보고 하는 것인데 그럴 적마다 나는 저만침 가서 ‘제에미 키두!’하고 논둑에다 침을 퉤, 뱉는다. 아무리 잘 봐야 내 겨드랑(다른 사람보다 좀 크긴 하지만) 밑에서 넘을락 말락 밤낮 요 모양이다.
paragraphs.en: Once I was so frustrated that I thought of going at her with a measuring stick and measuring that height just once. But my father-in-law says we must keep our distance as man and wife-to-be, so we never stand face to face and say so much as a word. Whenever we meet on the way to the well, I can only measure her by eye, and every time I walk on a little way and think, "Damn that height!" and spit on the ridge of the paddy. However well I look, it's always the same: she barely reaches, or just doesn't reach, the underside of my armpit (though I am a bit taller than other people).

paragraphs.orig: 개 돼지는 푹푹 크는데 왜 이리도 사람은 안 크는지, 한동안 머리가 아프도록 궁리도 해보았다. 아하, 물동이를 자꾸 이니까 뼉다귀가 움츠라드나보다, 하고 내가 넌즛넌즈시 그 물을 대신 길어도 주었다. 뿐만 아니라 나무를 하러 가면 서낭당에 돌을 올려 놓고 ‘점순이의 키 좀 크게 해줍소사. 그러면 담엔 떡 갖다 놓고 고사드립죠니까.’ 하고 치성도 한두 번 드린 것이 아니다. 어떻게 되먹은 킨지 이래도 막무가내니…….
paragraphs.en: Dogs and pigs shoot up, so why don't people grow? For a while I even racked my brain until my head ached. Ah, maybe it's because she keeps carrying the water jar on her head that her bones shrink, I thought, and on the quiet I even drew that water for her. Not only that, whenever I went to cut firewood I put a stone on the village shrine cairn and prayed, "Please make Jeom-sun's height grow a bit. Then next time I'll bring rice cake and give thanks," and I did that more than once or twice. What kind of height is it that it's still hopeless after all this...

paragraphs.orig: 그래 내 어저께 싸운 것이지 결코 장인님이 밉다든가 해서가 아니다.
paragraphs.en: So yesterday I picked a fight, but it was certainly not because I hate my father-in-law or anything of the kind.

paragraphs.orig: 모를 붓다가 가만히 생각을 해보니까 또 싱겁다. 이 벼가 자라서 점순이가 먹고 좀 큰다면 모르지만 그렇지도 못한 걸 내 심어서 뭘하는 거냐. 해마다 앞으로 축 불거지는 장인님의 아랫배(가 너무 먹는 걸 모르고 냇병이라나, 그 배)를 불리기 위하여 심곤 조금도 싶지 않다.
paragraphs.en: While planting out the seedlings I thought it over quietly and again it seemed pointless. If it were that Jeom-sun would eat this rice once it grew and get a bit bigger, that would be another thing, but what am I doing planting it when she won't? I don't feel at all like planting it just to feed my father-in-law's belly, which swells further forward every year (he doesn't know he eats too much and calls it a river sickness, that belly).

paragraphs.orig: “아이구 배야!”
paragraphs.en: "Ow, my stomach!"

paragraphs.orig: 난 몰 붓다 말고 배를 쓰다듬으면서도 그대루 논둑으로 기어올랐다. 그리고 겨드랑에 꼈던 벼 담긴 키를 그냥 땅바닥에 털썩 떨어치며 나도 털썩 주저앉았다. 일이 암만 바빠도 나 배 아프면 고만이니까. 아픈 사람이 누가 일을 하느냐. 파릇파릇 돋아오른 풀 한숲을 뜯어 들고 다리의 거머리를 쑥쑥 문대며 장인님의 얼굴을 쳐다보았다.
paragraphs.en: I broke off the planting and, stroking my belly, climbed up onto the ridge of the paddy all the same. And I dropped the winnowing basket full of rice seedlings I had tucked under my arm flat onto the ground, and plumped down myself. However busy the work, if my stomach hurts that's the end of it. What sick person works? I tore up a clump of fresh green grass and rubbed the leeches on my legs with it, and looked up at my father-in-law's face.

paragraphs.orig: 논 가운데서 장인님도 이상한 눈을 해가지고 한참 날 노려보더니,
paragraphs.en: From the middle of the paddy my father-in-law gave me a strange look and glared at me for a good while, then,

paragraphs.orig: “넌 이자식, 왜 또 이래 응?”
paragraphs.en: "You rascal, what's this again, eh?"

paragraphs.orig: “배가 좀 아파서유!”하고 풀 위에 슬며시 쓰러지니까 장인님은 약이 올랐다. 저도 논에서 철벙철벙 둑으로 올라오더니 잡은참 내 멱살을 움켜잡고 뺨을 치는 것이 아닌가……
paragraphs.en: "My stomach hurts a bit, sir!" I said, and quietly collapsed on the grass, which made my father-in-law furious. He came sloshing up out of the paddy onto the ridge, grabbed me by the collar right then and there and slapped my cheek...

paragraphs.orig: “이자식아. 일 허다 말면 누굴 망해놀 속셈이냐. 이 대가릴 까놀자식?”
paragraphs.en: "You rascal, if you stop work halfway, do you mean to ruin somebody? I'll split that skull of yours, you rascal!"

paragraphs.orig: 우리 장인님은 약이 오르면 이렇게 손버릇이 아주 못됐다. 또 사위에게 이자식 저자식 하는 이놈의 장인님은 어디 있느냐. 오죽해야 우리 동리에서 누굴 물론하고 그에게 욕을 안 먹는 사람은 명이 짜르다 한다. 조그만 아이들까지도 그를 돌아세놓고 욕필이(본 이름이 봉필이니까) 욕필이, 하고 손가락질을 할 만치 두루 인심을 잃었다. 허나 인심을 정말 잃었다면 욕보다 읍의 배참봉댁 마름으로 더 잃었다. 번히 마름이란 욕 잘하고, 사람 잘 치고, 그리고 생김생기길 호박개같애야 쓰는 거지만 장인님은 외양이 똑 됐다. 장인에게 닭마리나 좀 보내지 않는다든가 애벌논 때 품을 좀 안 준다든가 하면 그해 가을에는 영락없이 땅이 뚝뚝 떨어진다. 그러면 미리부터 돈도 먹고 술도 먹이고 안달재신으로 돌아치던 놈이 그 땅을 슬쩍 돌라 안는다. 이바람에 장인님집 외양간에는 눈깔 커다란 황소 한놈이 절로 엉금엉금 기어들고, 동리 사람들은 그 욕을 다 먹어가면서도 그래도 굽실굽실 하는 게 아닌가……
paragraphs.en: When my father-in-law gets angry, his hands are really bad like this. And where else is there a father-in-law who calls his son-in-law "rascal this, rascal that"? In our village they say that anyone who hasn't been cursed by him has a short life. Even little children have so lost their respect for him that they turn around and point at him and say, "Curse-Pil, Curse-Pil" (his real name is Bong-pil). But if you really come to losing respect, it's more as the steward for Squire Bae in town that he has lost it than for the cursing. By rights a steward has to be good at cursing, good at hitting people, and look like a squash-faced dog, and my father-in-law is exactly right in appearance. If you don't send him a hen now and then, or don't give him some labour at the first ploughing of his paddy, that autumn your land is sure to be taken away. Then the fellow who had been bustling about beforehand, bribing him with money and plying him with wine, quietly takes over that land. Because of this a big-eyed ox crawls into my father-in-law's stable all by itself, and the villagers, though they take all that cursing, still bow and scrape to him...

paragraphs.orig: 그러나 내겐 장인님이 감히 큰소리할 계제가 못된다.
paragraphs.en: But he is in no position to bellow at me.

paragraphs.orig: 뒷생각은 못하고 뺨 한 개를 딱 때려놓고는 장인님은 무색해서 덤덤히 쓴 침만 삼킨다. 난 그속을 퍽 잘 안다.
paragraphs.en: Without thinking of what comes after, he slaps my cheek once, then he's embarrassed, and just swallows his bitter spit in silence. I know very well what's going on in his mind.

paragraphs.orig: 조금 있으면 갈도 꺾어야 하고 모도 내야 하고, 한참 바쁜 때인데 나 일 안하고 우리집으로 그냥 가면 고만이니까.
paragraphs.en: Soon it will be time to cut green manure and transplant the rice, the busiest season, and if I stop working and just go home, that's the end of it.

paragraphs.orig: 작년 이맘때도 트집을 좀 하니까 늦잠잔다구 돌멩이를 집어던져서 자는 놈의 발목을 삐게 해놨다. 사날씩이나 건숭 끙끙, 앓았더니 종당에는 거반 울상이 되지 않았는가……
paragraphs.en: At this time last year too I started some trouble, and he threw a stone at me for sleeping late and hit the sleeping fellow's ankle and sprained it. I groaned and moaned for show for three or four days, until in the end he was nearly in tears...

paragraphs.orig: “예, 그만 일어나 일 좀 해라. 그래야 올 갈에 벼 잘되면 너 장가 들지 않니.”
paragraphs.en: "Come, get up now and do some work. Then if the rice does well this autumn, you'll get married, won't you."

paragraphs.orig: 그래 귀가 번쩍 띄어서 그날로 일어나서 남이 이틀 품들일 논을 혼자 삶아 놓으니까 장인님도 눈깔이 커다랗게 놀랐다. 그럼 정말로 가을에 와서 혼인을 시켜 줘야 온 경우가 옳지 않겠나, 볏섬을 척척 들여쌓아도 다른 소리는 없고 물동이를 이고 들어오는 점순이를 담배통으로 가리키며, “이 자식아, 미처 커야지 조걸 무슨 혼인을 한다구 그러니 원!”하고 남 낯짝만 붉혀 주고 고만이다.
paragraphs.en: So my ears pricked up, and that very day I got up and single-handedly puddled a paddy that would take another man two days' labour, and my father-in-law's eyes widened. Then surely, when autumn came, it would only be right to marry us off for real, but even after the rice sacks were piled up in rows there was not a different word, and pointing with his pipe at Jeom-sun coming in carrying a water jar on her head, he said, "You rascal, she has to grow first, what's this about marrying that one?" and all he did was make my face go red, and that was that.

paragraphs.orig: 골김에 그저 이놈의 장인님, 하고 댓돌에다 메꼰코 우리 고향으로 내뺄까 하다가 꾹꾹 참고 말았다.
paragraphs.en: In my anger I thought of just saying "you wretched father-in-law," and flinging him down on the stone step and bolting back to my home village, but I gritted my teeth and held it in.

paragraphs.orig: 참말이지 난 이꼴하고는 집으로 차마 못 간다. 장가를 들러갔다가 오죽 못났어야 그대로 쫓겨왔느냐고 손가락질을 받을 테니까…….
paragraphs.en: Really, I can't possibly go home looking like this. They'd point at me and say that I must have been truly worthless to go to get married and be chased back like that...

paragraphs.orig: 논둑에서 벌떡 일어나 한풀 죽은 장인님 앞으로 다가서며,
paragraphs.en: I jumped up from the ridge and walked up to my father-in-law, who had lost some of his spirit, and said,

paragraphs.orig: “난 갈 테야유. 그동안 사경 쳐내슈.”
paragraphs.en: "I'm leaving. Pay me my wages for all this time."

paragraphs.orig: “너 사위로 왔지 어디 머슴살러 왔니?”
paragraphs.en: "You came as a son-in-law, not to work as a hired hand, did you?"

paragraphs.orig: “그러면 얼찐 성례를 해줘야 안하지유. 밤낮 부려만 먹구 해준다, 해준다……”
paragraphs.en: "Then you should hurry up and hold the wedding, shouldn't you? You just use me day and night, saying you will, you will..."

paragraphs.orig: “글쎄, 내가 안하는 거냐, 그년이 안 크니까.”하고 어름어름 담배만 담으면서 늘 하는 소리를 또 늘어놓는다.
paragraphs.en: "Well, am I not doing it? It's that girl who won't grow," he said, fumbling to fill his pipe and spinning out the same old line he always uses.

paragraphs.orig: 이렇게 따져나가면 언제든지 늘 나만 밑지고 만다. 이번엔 안 된다, 하고 대뜸 구장님한테로 판단 가자고 소맷자락을 내끌었다.
paragraphs.en: If I argue it out like this, it always ends with me on the losing side. Not this time, I thought, and straight away I pulled at his sleeve to go and have the village headman judge.

paragraphs.orig: “아, 이자식이 왜 이래 어른을.”
paragraphs.en: "Hey, why is this rascal doing this to an elder?"

paragraphs.orig: 안 간다구 뻗디디구 이렇게 호령은 제맘대로 하지만 장인님 제가 내 기운은 못 당한다. 막 부려먹고 딸은 안 주고, 게다 땅땅 치는 건 다 뭐야…….
paragraphs.en: He dug in his heels saying he wouldn't go and bellowed commands as he liked, but he's no match for my strength. Working me to the bone and not giving me his daughter, and on top of that hitting me, what is all this...

paragraphs.orig: ## 2. 점순이의 재촉과 구장님
paragraphs.en: 2. Jeom-sun's Urging and the Headman

paragraphs.orig: 그러나 내 사실 참 장인님이 미워서 그런 것은 아니다. 그 전날, 왜 내가 새고 개 맞은 봉우리 화전밭을 혼자 갈고 있지 않았느냐. 밭가생이로 돌 적마다 야릇한 꽃내가 물컥물컥 코를 찌르고 머리 위에서 벌들은 가끔 붕, 붕, 소리를 친다. 바위 틈에서 샘물 소리밖에 안 들리는 산골짜기니까 맑은 하늘의 봄볕은 이불 속같이 따스하고 꼭 꿈꾸는 것 같다. 나는 몸이 나른하고 몸살(병을 아직 모르지만)이 날려구 그러는지 가슴이 울렁울렁하고 이랬다.
paragraphs.en: But really it wasn't that I hated my father-in-law. The day before, hadn't I been ploughing alone the burnt-field plot on the peak across the pass? Every time I turned at the edge of the field, a strange scent of flowers hit my nose in gusts, and above my head the bees sometimes went buzz, buzz. It was a mountain valley where you heard nothing but the sound of a spring from among the rocks, so the spring sunshine from the clear sky was warm as inside a quilt, just as if I were dreaming. My body was languid, and maybe I was about to come down with an illness (though I still don't know what illness is), because my heart was pounding.

paragraphs.orig: “어러이! 말이! 맘 마 마……”
paragraphs.en: "Gee up! Horse! Mam ma ma..."

paragraphs.orig: 이렇게 노래를 하며 소를 부리면 여느때 같으면 어깨가 으쓱으쓱한다. 웬일인지 밭을 반도 갈지 않아서 온몸이 맥이 풀리고 대구 짜증만 난다. 공연히 소만 들입다 두들기며……
paragraphs.en: Normally when I sing like this and drive the ox, my shoulders sway with it. For some reason, before I had ploughed even half the field all the strength went out of my body and I was only irritated all the time. I beat the ox hard for no reason...

paragraphs.orig: “안야! 안야! 이 망할 자식의 소(장인님의 소니까) 대리를 꺾어들라.”
paragraphs.en: "Get along! Get along! Break the head off that damned fellow's ox (it's my father-in-law's ox)."

paragraphs.orig: 그러나 내 속은 정말 안야 때문이 아니라 점심을 이고 온 점순이의 키를 보고 울화가 났던 것이다.
paragraphs.en: But what really made me angry was not the ox, it was seeing the height of Jeom-sun, who had come carrying my lunch on her head.

paragraphs.orig: 점순이는 뭐 그리 썩 예쁜 계집애는 못된다. 그렇다구 또 개떡이냐 하면 그런 것도 아니고, 꼭 내 아내가 돼야 할 만치 그저 툽툽하게 생긴 얼굴이다. 나보다 십년이 아래니까 올해 열여섯인데 몸은 남보다 두 살이나 덜 자랐다. 남은 잘도 훤칠히들 크건만 이건 위아래가 뭉툭한 것이 내 눈에는 헐없이 감참외 같다. 참외 중에는 감참외가 제일 맛좋고 예쁘니까 말이다. 둥글고 커다란 눈은 서글서글하니 좋고 좀 지쳐 찢어졌지만 입은 밥술이나 톡톡히 먹음직하니 좋다. 아따, 밥만 많이 먹게 되면 팔자는 고만 아니냐. 헌데 한 가지 과가 있다면 가끔가다 몸이(장인님이 이걸 채신이 없이 들까분다고 하지만)너무 빨리빨리 논다. 그래서 밥을 나르다가 때없이 풀밭에서 깨빡을 쳐서 흙투성이 밥을 곧잘 먹인다. 안 먹으면 무안해 할까봐서 이걸 씹고 앉았느라면 으적으적 소리만 나고 돌을 먹는 겐지 밥을 먹는 겐지…….
paragraphs.en: Jeom-sun is not what you'd call a very pretty girl. Still, it isn't that she's a dumpling either: she has a plain, sturdy face, just right for a wife of mine. She's ten years younger than I am, so she's sixteen this year, but her body is two years behind others'. Other girls grow up nicely tall, but she is stumpy top to bottom and to my eyes she's simply like a golden melon. Among melons the golden melon tastes best and looks prettiest, you see. Her big round eyes are kind and good, and her mouth, though a bit wide and slit, looks like it could eat a good bowl of rice. Well, if she can eat plenty of rice, her fortune is made. If there's one fault, it's that now and then her body moves too fast (my father-in-law says she's flighty and has no dignity). So while bringing the meal she tumbles on the grass at all times, and often feeds me rice covered in dirt. If I didn't eat it she'd be embarrassed, so I sit chewing it with a crunch crunch sound, and it's hard to tell if I'm eating stones or rice...

paragraphs.orig: 그러나 이날은 웬일인지 성한 밥채루 밭머리에 곱게 내려 놓았다. 그리고 또 내외를 해야 하니까 저만큼 떨어져 이쪽으로 등을 향하고 웅크리고 앉아서 그릇나기를 기다린다.
paragraphs.en: But that day, for some reason, she set down the meal in one piece at the edge of the field. Then, since we have to keep our distance, she crouched a good way off with her back to me, waiting for the dishes.

paragraphs.orig: 내가 다 먹고 물러섰을 때, 그릇을 챙기는데 난 깜짝 놀라지 않았느냐. 고개를 푹 숙이고 밥함지에 그릇을 포개면서 날더러 들으라는지, 혹은 제 소린지,
paragraphs.en: When I had finished eating and stepped back, and she was gathering up the dishes, wasn't I startled! With her head bowed low, stacking the bowls in the rice tub, whether for me to hear or just talking to herself,

paragraphs.orig: "밤낮 일만 하다 말 텐가!"
paragraphs.en: "Are you going to do nothing but work, day in and day out!"

paragraphs.orig: 하고 혼자서 쫑알거린다. 고대 잘 내외하다가 이게 무슨 소린가, 하고 난 정신이 얼떨떨했다. 그러면서도 한편 무슨 좋은 수가 있나 없는가 싶어서 나도 공중을 대고 혼잣말로,
paragraphs.en: she muttered to herself. She had been keeping her distance so well just now, what is this, I thought, and my mind was in a whirl. Yet at the same time, wondering whether there might be some good way out, I too spoke into the air, to myself,

paragraphs.orig: "그럼 어떡해?"
paragraphs.en: "Then what should I do?"

paragraphs.orig: 하니까,
paragraphs.en: and she said,

paragraphs.orig: "성례시켜 달라지 뭘 어떡해."
paragraphs.en: "Ask them to hold the wedding, what else should you do."

paragraphs.orig: 하고 되알지게 쏘아붙이고 얼굴이 빨개져서 산으로 그저 도망친다.
paragraphs.en: She snapped this out sharply, her face turned red, and she simply fled up the mountain.

paragraphs.orig: 나는 잠시 동안 어떻게 되는 심판인지 맥을 몰라서 그 뒷모양만 덤덤히 바라보았다.
paragraphs.en: For a while I didn't understand what on earth was going on, and just stared blankly at her retreating figure.

paragraphs.orig: 봄이 되면 온갖 초목이 물이 오르고 싹이 트고 한다. 사람도 아마 그런가 보다, 하고 며칠내에 부쩍 (속으로) 자란 듯싶은 점순이가 여간 반가운 것이 아니다. 이런 걸 멀쩡하게 아직 어리다구 하니까…….
paragraphs.en: When spring comes, all the plants and trees get sap and sprout. People must be like that too, I thought, and I was very glad to see Jeom-sun, who seemed to have grown a great deal in the last few days (inside). And here they insist she's still young...

paragraphs.orig: 우리가 구장님을 찾아갔을 때 그는 싸리문 밖에 있는 돼지우리에서 죽을 퍼주고 있었다. 서울엘 좀 갔다오더니 사람은 점잖아야 한다구 웃쇰이(얼른 보면 지붕 위에 앉은 제비꼬랑지 같다) 양쪽으로 뾰죽히 삐치고 그걸 애헴, 하고 늘 쓰담는 손버릇이 있다.
paragraphs.en: When we went to see the village headman, he was in the pigsty outside the brushwood gate, ladling out slop. Since he went to Seoul and came back, he says a man must be dignified, and his upper moustache (at first glance it looks like a swallow's tail sitting on a roof) juts out sharply on both sides, and he has a habit of stroking it with an "ahem!"

paragraphs.orig: 우리를 멀뚱히 쳐다보고 미리 알아챘는지,
paragraphs.en: He stared at us blankly, as if he had guessed it beforehand,

paragraphs.orig: "왜 일들 허다 말구 그래?"하더니 손을 올려서 그 애헴을 한번 후딱 했다.
paragraphs.en: "Why have you two stopped your work?" he said, and quickly raised his hand and gave that "ahem."

paragraphs.orig: "구장님! 우리 장인님과 츰에 계약하기를……"
paragraphs.en: "Village headman! When we first made the contract with my father-in-law..."

paragraphs.orig: 먼저 덤비는 장인님을 뒤로 떠다밀고 내가 허둥지둥 달려들다가 가만히 생각하고, '아니 우리 빙장님과 츰에.'하고 첫번부터 다시 말을 고쳤다. 장인님은 빙장님, 해야 좋아하고 밖에 나와서 장인님, 하면 괜스리 골을 내려고 든다. 뱀두 뱀이래야 좋으냐구 창피스러우니 남 듣는 데는 제발 빙장님, 빙모님, 하라구 일상 당조심을 받아오면서 난 그것두 자꾸 잊는다.
paragraphs.en: I pushed my father-in-law, who was rushing in first, aside and charged in in a flurry, then thought it over and corrected myself, "No, when we first made it with my honoured father-in-law," and started again from the beginning. My father-in-law likes to be called "Honoured Father-in-law" and if I say the plain "father-in-law" outside the house, he looks ready to fly into a temper for nothing. "Does even a snake like being called a snake?" he says, and since it's embarrassing, I'm always warned that in front of others I must please say "Honoured Father-in-law, Honoured Mother-in-law," and I keep forgetting even that.

paragraphs.orig: 당장두 장인님, 하나 옆에서 내 발등을 꾹 밟고 곁눈질을 흘기는 바람에야 겨우 알았지만……
paragraphs.en: Just now too I said the plain "father-in-law", and only realised when he stepped hard on the top of my foot from beside me and glared sideways...

paragraphs.orig: 구장님도 내 이야기를 자세히 듣더니 퍽 딱한 모양이었다. 하기야 구장님뿐만 아니라 누구든지 다 그럴 게다.
paragraphs.en: The village headman listened carefully to my story and seemed quite sorry for me. Well, not only the headman, anyone would be.

paragraphs.orig: 길게 길러둔 새끼손톱으로 코를 후벼서 저리 탁 튀기며,
paragraphs.en: With his long-grown little fingernail he dug at his nose, flicked it away, and said,

paragraphs.orig: "그럼 봉필씨! 얼른 성례를 시켜 주구려, 그렇게까지 제가 하구싶다는 걸……"
paragraphs.en: "Well then, Mr. Bong-pil, hold the wedding quickly, when the boy wants it that badly..."

paragraphs.orig: 하고 내 짐작대로 말했다. 그러나 이말에 장인님이 삿대질로 눈을 부라리고,
paragraphs.en: just as I expected. But at this my father-in-law glared, jabbing the air with his finger,

paragraphs.orig: "아 성례구 뭐구 계집애년이 미처 자라야 할 게 아닌가?"
paragraphs.en: "Ah, wedding, my foot, doesn't the girl have to grow first?"

paragraphs.orig: 하니까 고만 멀쑤룩해져서 입맛만 쩍쩍 다실 뿐이 아닌가.
paragraphs.en: and the headman was left looking foolish, merely smacking his lips.

paragraphs.orig: "그것두 그래!"
paragraphs.en: "That's true too!"

paragraphs.orig: "그래, 거진 사년 동안에도 안 자랐더니 그 킨 은제 자라지유"다 그만두구 사경 내슈……"
paragraphs.en: "Well, she hasn't grown in nearly four years, so when will that height ever grow? Forget it, pay me my wages..."

paragraphs.orig: "글쎄, 이자식아! 내가 크질 말라구 그랬니. 왜 날 보구 떼냐?"
paragraphs.en: "Well, you rascal! Did I tell her not to grow? Why are you blaming me?"

paragraphs.orig: "빙모님은 참새만한 것이 그럼 어떻게 앨 낳지유?(사실 빙모님은점순이보다도 귓배기가 작다)"
paragraphs.en: "My mother-in-law is the size of a sparrow, so how did she have a child?" (In truth, my mother-in-law has even smaller ears than Jeom-sun.)

paragraphs.orig: 장인님은 이말을 듣고 껄껄 웃더니(그러나 암만 해두 돌 씹은 상이다) 코를 푸는 척하고 날 은근히 곯리려고 팔꿈치로 옆 갈비께를 퍽 치는 것이다.
paragraphs.en: My father-in-law heard this and roared with laughter (though he certainly had a face like he was chewing stones), and pretending to blow his nose, he drove his elbow hard into my side ribs, meaning to quietly get the better of me.

paragraphs.orig: 더럽다. 나두 종아리의 파리를 쫓는 척하고 허리를 구부리며 그 궁둥이를 콱 떼밀었다. 장인님은 앞으로 우찔근하고 싸리문께로 쓰러질 듯하다 몸을 바로 고치더니 눈총을 몹시 쏘았다. 이런 쌍년의 자식, 하곤 싶으나 남의 앞이라니 차마 못하고 섰는 그 꼴이 보기에 퍽 쟁그러웠다.
paragraphs.en: Dirty trick. I too pretended to shoo a fly off my calf, bent over, and shoved his rump hard. My father-in-law lurched forward and nearly fell toward the brushwood gate, then straightened himself and shot me a fierce look. He wanted to say "you son of a bitch," but couldn't bring himself to do it in front of someone else, and the sight of him standing there was very funny.

paragraphs.orig: 그러나 이밖에는 별반 신통한 귀정을 얻지 못하고 도로 논으로 돌아와서 모를 부었다. 왜냐면 장인님이 뭐라구 귓속말로 수군수군하고 간 뒤다. 구장님이 날 위해서 조용히 데리고 아래와 같이 일러주었기 때문이다(뭉태의 말은 구장님이 장인님에게 땅 두 마지기 얻어부치니까 그래 꾀엿다고 하지만 난 그렇게 생각 않는다)
paragraphs.en: But apart from that there was no particularly good settlement, and I went back to the paddy and went on planting. Because after my father-in-law whispered something in his ear and left, the village headman quietly took me aside and told me as follows (Mungtae says the headman did it because he rents two plots of land from my father-in-law, but I don't think so).

paragraphs.orig: "자네 말두 하기야 옳지, 암 나이 찼으니 아들이 급하다는 게 잘못된 말은 아니야. 허지만 농사가 한층 바쁜 때 일을 안한다든가집으로 달아 난다든가 하면 손해죄루 그것두 징역을 가거든!(여기에 그만 정신이 번쩍 났다) 왜 요전에 삼포말서 산에 불좀 놓았다구 징역간 거 못 봤나. 제 산에 불을 놓아도 징역을 가는 이땐데 남의 농사를 버려두니 죄가 얼마나 더 중한가. 그리고 자넨 정장을(사경 받으러 정장 가겠다 했다) 간대지만 그러면 괜스리 죄를 들쓰고 들어가는 걸세. 또 결혼두 그렇지. 법률에 성년이란 게 있는데 스물하나가 돼야지 비로소 결혼을 할 수가 있는걸세. 자넨 물론 아들이 늦을 걸 염려하지만 점순이루 말하면 이제 겨우 열여섯이 아닌가. 그렇지만 아까 빙장님의 말씀이 올 갈에는 열일을 제치고라두 성례를 시켜주겠다 하시니 좀 고마울겐가. 빨리 가서 모붓든 거나 마저 붓게, 군소리 말구 어서 가."
paragraphs.en: "Well, you're right, of course. You're of age, so it isn't wrong to be impatient for a son. But if at the busiest farming time you don't work or run home, that's damage and a crime, and for that you can go to prison too! (At this I snapped to attention.) Didn't you see the other day that a man from Sampo-mal went to prison for setting a fire on a mountain? Nowadays you go to prison even for setting fire to your own mountain, so how much worse is the crime of abandoning somebody else's farming. And you say you'll go to court (I had said I would go to court to get my wages), but then you would only take on blame for nothing and be put in. As for marriage too: the law has what's called adulthood, and you can't marry until you're twenty-one. Of course you worry that a son will come late, but as for Jeom-sun, she's only sixteen now, isn't she? Even so, the Honoured Father-in-law said just now that this autumn he'll put everything else aside and hold the wedding, so shouldn't you be a little grateful? Go quickly and finish planting what you were planting, no more grumbling, go on.

paragraphs.orig: 그래서 오늘 아침까지 끽소리 없이 왔다.
paragraphs.en: And so I had gone along without a peep until this morning.

paragraphs.orig: ## 3. 뭉태의 이야기
paragraphs.en: 3. What Mungtae Said

paragraphs.orig: 장인님과 내가 싸운 것은 지금 생각하면 전혀 뜻밖의 일이라 안할 수 없다.
paragraphs.en: Thinking about it now, I can't help saying that the fight between my father-in-law and me was completely unexpected.

paragraphs.orig: 장인님으로 말하면 요즈막 작인들에게 행세를 좀 하고 싶다고 해서,
paragraphs.en: As for my father-in-law, lately he's wanted to throw his weight around with his tenants a bit,

paragraphs.orig: "돈 있으면 양반이지 별게 있느냐!"
paragraphs.en: "If you have money you're a gentleman, what else is there!"

paragraphs.orig: 하고 일부러 아랫배를 쑥 내밀고 걸음도 뒤틀리게 걷고 하는 이판이다. 이까진 나쯤 두들기다 남의 땅을 가지고 모처럼 닦아놓았던 가문을 망친다든가 할 어른이 아니다. 또 나로 논지면 아무쪼록 잘 봬서 점순이에게 얼른 장가를 들어야 하지 않느냐…….
paragraphs.en: and he deliberately sticks out his belly and walks with a swagger. He is not the sort of elder who would beat the likes of me and ruin the family name he has taken such pains to polish on other people's land. And as for me, I have to make myself look as good as possible and marry Jeom-sun quickly, don't I...

paragraphs.orig: 이렇게 말하자면 결국 어젯밤 뭉태네 집에 마슬간 것이 썩 나빴다. 낮에 구장님 앞에서 장인님과 내가 싸운 것을 어떻게 알았는지 대구 빈정거리는 것이 아닌가.
paragraphs.en: If I put it that way, in the end it was very bad that last night I went visiting at Mungtae's house. Somehow he'd found out that my father-in-law and I had fought in front of the village headman in the daytime, and he kept sneering.

paragraphs.orig: "그래 맞구두 그걸 가만 둬?"
paragraphs.en: "So you got hit and you let it go?"

paragraphs.orig: "그럼 어떡허니?"
paragraphs.en: "Then what should I do?"

paragraphs.orig: "임마, 봉필일 모판에다 거꾸로 박아놓지 뭘 어떡해?"하고 괜히 내 대신 화를 내가지고 주먹질을 하다 등잔까지 쳤다. 놈이 번히 괄괄은 하지만 그래놓고 날더러 석유값을 물라구 막 찌다우를 붙는다. 난 어안이 벙벙해서 잠자코 앉았으니까 저만 연신 지껄이는 소리가,
paragraphs.en: "You idiot, just stick Bong-pil head-first in the seedbed, what else?" he said, getting angry in my place for no reason, and in waving his fists he even knocked over the lamp. He's always been hot-tempered, but having done that, he pestered me to pay for the kerosene. I sat there in silence, dumbfounded, while he kept on chattering,

paragraphs.orig: "밤낮 일만 해주구 있을 테냐?"
paragraphs.en: "Are you going to keep working for him day and night?"

paragraphs.orig: "영득이는 일년을 살구두 장갈 들었는데 넌 사년이나 살구두 더살아야 해?"
paragraphs.en: "Yeong-deuk married after living there one year, and you've lived there four years and have to live there more?"

paragraphs.orig: "네가 세번째 사윈줄이나 아니? 세번째 사위"
paragraphs.en: "Do you know you're the third son-in-law? The third!"

paragraphs.orig: "남의 일이라두 분하다. 이자식아, 우물에 가 빠져 죽어."
paragraphs.en: "Even if it's another man's affair, it makes me furious. You rascal, go and drown yourself in the well."

paragraphs.orig: 나중에는 겨우 손톱으로 목을 따라고까지 하고, 제 아들같이 함부로 훅닥이었다. 별의별 소리를 다해서 그대로 옮길 수는 없으나 그 줄거리는 이렇다…….
paragraphs.en: In the end he even said to slit my throat with my fingernail, and bullied me roughly as if I were his own son. He said all sorts of things that I can't repeat as they were, but the gist was this...

paragraphs.orig: 우리 장인님 딸이 셋이 있는데 맏딸은 재작년 가을에 시집을 갔다. 정말은 시집을 간 것이 아니라 그 딸도 데릴사위를 해가지고 있다가 내보냈다. 그런데 딸이 열 살 때부터 열아홉 즉 십년 동안에 데릴사위를 갈아들이기를, 동리에선 사위부자라고 이름이 났지마는 열네 놈이란 참 너무 많다. 장인님이 아들은 없고 딸만 있는 고로 그담 딸을 데릴사위를 해올 때까지는 부려먹지 않으면 안된다. 물론 머슴을 두면 좋지만 그건 돈이 드니까, 일 잘하는 놈을 고르느라고 연방 바꿔들였다. 또 한편 놈들이 욕만 줄창 퍼붓고 심히도 부려먹으니까 밸이 상해서 달아나기도 했겠지, 점순이는 둘째딸인데 내가 일테면 그 세번째 데릴사위로 들어온 셈이다. 내 담으로 네번째 놈이 들어올 것을 내가 일도 잘하고 그리고 사람이 좀 어수록하니까 장인님이 잔뜩 붙들고 놓질 않는다. 세째딸이 인제 여섯살, 적어두 열 살은 돼야 데릴사위를 할 테므로 그 동안은 죽도록 부려먹어야 된다. 그러니 인제는 속 좀 채리고 장가를 들여달라구 떼를 쓰고 나자빠져라, 이것이다.
paragraphs.en: My father-in-law has three daughters, and the eldest married out the autumn before last. In truth she did not marry out; that daughter too had a resident son-in-law who was sent away. From when the daughter was ten to nineteen, that is, in ten years, he took in and swapped out resident sons-in-law until in the village he became known as a rich man in sons-in-law, but fourteen of them is really far too many. Since my father-in-law has no son, only daughters, he has to work them until the next daughter's resident son-in-law comes. Of course it would be good to hire a farmhand, but that costs money, so he kept swapping them in order to choose ones who work well. On the other side, the fellows were cursed constantly and worked terribly hard, so they must have got sick of it and run away. Jeom-sun is the second daughter, and I came in as, so to speak, her third resident son-in-law. A fourth fellow should have come in after me, but because I work well and am a bit simple, my father-in-law has a tight grip on me and won't let go. The third daughter is six now, and he can't take a resident son-in-law until she's at least ten, so until then he has to work me to death. So now pull yourself together and throw yourself down and make a scene demanding he marry you off, that's what he said.

paragraphs.orig: 나는 겉으로 엉, 엉, 하며 귓등으로 들었다. 뭉태는 땅을 얻어부치다가 떨어진 뒤로는 장인님만 보면 공연히 못 먹어서 으릉거린다. 그것도 장인님이 저 달라고 할 적에 제 집에서 위한다는 그 감투(예전에 원님이 쓰던 것이라나, 옆구리에 뽕뽕 좀 먹은 걸레)를 선뜻 주었더면 그럴 리도 없었던 걸…….
paragraphs.en: Outwardly I said "uh-huh, uh-huh" and listened with the back of my ear. Mungtae, ever since he rented land from my father-in-law and lost it, growls at him for nothing whenever he sees him, because he got nothing to eat. Even that wouldn't have happened if my father-in-law had asked for it and Mungtae had readily handed over the cap his family prized (it was supposedly worn by a magistrate long ago, a rag moth-eaten at the sides)...

paragraphs.orig: 그러나 나는 뭉태란 놈의 말을 전수히 곧이듣지 않았다. 꼭 곧이들었다면 간밤에 와서 장인님과 싸웠지 무사히 있었을 리가 없지 않은가. 그러면 딸에게까지 인심을 잃은 장인님이 혼자 나빴다.
paragraphs.en: But I didn't believe everything that fellow Mungtae said. If I really had, I would have come last night and fought with my father-in-law, and it couldn't have passed peacefully. So my father-in-law, who has lost respect even among his daughters, was the only bad one.

paragraphs.orig: ## 4. 다시 꾀병
paragraphs.en: 4. Playing Sick Again

paragraphs.orig: 실토이지 나는 점순이가 아침상을 가지고 나올 때까지는 오늘은 또 얼마나 밥을 담았나, 하고 이것만 생각했다. 상에는 된장찌개하고 간장 한 종지, 조밥 한 그릇, 그리고 밥보다 더 수부룩하게 담은 산나물이 한 대접, 이렇다. 나물은 점순이가 틈틈이 해오니까 두 대접이고 네 대접이고 멋대로 먹어도 좋으나 밥은 장인님이 한 사발 외엔 더 주지 말라고 해서 안된다. 그런데 점순이가 그 상을 내 앞에 내려 놓으며 제 말로 지껄이는 소리가,
paragraphs.en: To tell the truth, until Jeom-sun came out with the breakfast tray, I thought only about how much rice she had dished up today. On the tray there was bean paste stew, a small dish of soy sauce, a bowl of millet rice, and a large bowl of wild greens piled even more bushily than the rice. Jeom-sun brings the greens now and then, so I can eat two bowls or four as I like, but as for the rice, my father-in-law has said I'm not to be given more than one bowl. And Jeom-sun set that tray in front of me and chattered, in her own words,

paragraphs.orig: "구장님한테 갔다 그냥 온담 그래!"하고 엊그제 산에서와 같이 되우 쫑알거린다. 딴은 내가 더 단단히 덤비지 않고 만 것이 좀 어리석었다, 속으로 그랬다.
paragraphs.en: "If you went to the headman and just came back like that, then what!" she said, scolding hard just like the other day on the mountain. Indeed, it had been a bit foolish of me not to press harder, I thought to myself.

paragraphs.orig: 나도 저쪽 벽을 향하여 외면하면서 내 말로,
paragraphs.en: I also turned my face away toward the far wall and said, in my own words,

paragraphs.orig: "안된다는 걸 그럼 어떡헌담!"하니까,
paragraphs.en: "But he said no, so what can I do!"

paragraphs.orig: "쇰을 잡아채지 그냥 둬, 이 바보야!"
paragraphs.en: "Grab his whiskers, why leave him alone, you fool!"

paragraphs.orig: 하고 또 얼굴이 빨개지면서 성을 내며 안으로 샐죽하니 튀들어가지 않느냐, 이때 아무도 본 사람이 없었게 망정이지 보았다면 내 얼굴이 에미 잃은 황새새끼처럼 가여 웁다 했을 것이다.
paragraphs.en: she said, and her face went red again, and angrily she darted back inside. At that moment nobody saw it, luckily; if anyone had, they would have said my face looked as pitiful as a stork chick that has lost its mother.

paragraphs.orig: 사실 이때만치 슬펐던 일이 또 있었는지 모른다. 다른 사람은 암만 못생겼다 해두 괜찮지만 내 아내 될 점순이가 병신으로 본다면 참 신세는 따분하다. 밥을 먹은 뒤 지게를 지고 일터로 갈려 하다 도로 벗어던지고 바깥 마당 공석 위에 드러누워서 나는 차라리 죽느니만 같지 못하다 생각했다.
paragraphs.en: I don't know whether there was ever a time as sad as this. It would be all right for any other person to call me hopeless, but if Jeom-sun, who is to be my wife, takes me for a dolt, then my lot is miserable. After the meal I took up my A-frame and was about to go to the work-site, but threw it off again and lay down on the straw mat in the outer yard, thinking I might as well die.

paragraphs.orig: 내가 일 안하면 장인님 저는 나이가 먹어 못하고 결국 농사 못 짓고 만다. 뒷짐으로 트림을 꿀꺽하고 대문 밖으로 나오다 날 보고서,
paragraphs.en: If I don't work, my father-in-law is too old to do it himself, and in the end the farming won't get done. With his hands behind his back and a loud belch, he came out of the gate, saw me, and said,

paragraphs.orig: "이자식아, 왜 또 이러니."
paragraphs.en: "You rascal, what's this again?"

paragraphs.orig: "관격이 났어유, 아이구 배야!"
paragraphs.en: "I've got a seizure, ow, my stomach!"

paragraphs.orig: "기껀 밥 처먹구 무슨 관격이야, 남의 농사 버려주면 이자식아 징역간다 봐라!"
paragraphs.en: "What seizure after stuffing yourself with rice? If you ruin someone else's farming, you rascal, you'll go to prison, mark my words!"

paragraphs.orig: "가두 좋아유, 아이구 배야!"
paragraphs.en: "I don't mind, ow, my stomach!"

paragraphs.orig: 참말 난 일 안해서 징역 가도 좋다 생각했다. 일후 아들을 낳아도 그 앞에서 바보, 바보, 이렇게 별명을 들을 테니까 오늘은 열쪽이 난대도 결정을 내고 싶었다.
paragraphs.en: I really did think I wouldn't mind going to prison for not working. Even if I later have a son, he will call me idiot, idiot to my face, so today, even if I were split in ten pieces, I wanted to settle it.

paragraphs.orig: 장인님이 일어나라고 해도 내가 안 일어나니까 눈에 독이 올라서 저편으로 힝하게 가더니 지게막대기를 들고 왔다. 그리고 그걸로 내 허리를 마치 돌 떠넘기듯이 쿡 찍어서 넘기고 넘기고 했다. 밥을 잔뜩 먹어 딱딱한 배가 그럴 적마다 퉁겨지면서 밸창이 꼿꼿한 것이 여간 켕기지 않았다. 그래도 안 일어나니까 이번에는 배를 지게 막대기로 위에서 쿡쿡 찌르고 발길로 옆구리를 차고 했다. 장인님은 원체 심청이 궂어서 그러지만 나도 저만 못하지 않게 배를 채었다. 아픈 것을 눈을 꽉 감고 넌 해라 난 재밌단 듯이 있었으나 볼기짝을 후려갈길 적에는 나도 모르는 결에 벌떡 일어나서 그 수염을 잡아챘다. 마는 내 골이 난 것이 아니라 정말은 아까부터 벽 뒤 울타리 구멍으로 점순이가 우리들의 꼴을 몰래 엿보고 있었기 때문이다.
paragraphs.en: My father-in-law told me to get up, but I didn't, and his eyes filled with venom; he went off briskly and came back with an A-frame pole. And with that he jabbed my waist as if rolling a stone over, and rolled me over, again and again. My belly, tight and hard from all the rice, bounced each time, and my intestines were stiff and strained. When I still didn't get up, he jabbed my belly from above with the pole and kicked my ribs. My father-in-law does it because he's so mean-spirited, but I braced my belly no less than he did. I shut my eyes tight against the pain and acted as if I thought, you go ahead, I'm enjoying this, but when he lashed my buttocks I jumped up before I knew it and grabbed his whiskers. But it wasn't that I lost my temper; the real reason was that all this time Jeom-sun had been secretly peeking at our state through a hole in the fence behind the wall.

paragraphs.orig: 가뜩이나 말 한마디 톡톡히 못한다고 바라보는데 매까지 잠자코 맞는 걸 보면 짜장 바보로 알 게 아닌가. 또 점순이도 미워하는 이까짓 놈의 장인님하곤 아무것도 안되니까 막 때려도 좋지만 사정 보아서 수염만 채고(제 원대로 했으니까 이때 점순이는 퍽 기뻤겠지) 저기까지 잘 들리도록 '이걸 까셀라부다!'하고 소리를 쳤다.
paragraphs.en: She already looked at me as someone who can't even say a firm word, and if she saw me quietly taking a beating too, she would surely take me for a real idiot. Besides, since this father-in-law whom even Jeom-sun hates is nothing to me, I could have hit him all I liked, but weighing the circumstances I only pulled his whiskers (since she got what she wanted, Jeom-sun must have been very pleased just then) and shouted loudly enough for her to hear, "I'll pluck them out!"

paragraphs.orig: 장인님은 더 약이 바짝 올라서 잡은 참 지게막대기로 내 어깨를 그냥 내려갈겼다. 정신이 다 아찔하다. 다시 고개를 들었을 때 그때엔 나도 온몸에 약이 올랐다. 이녀석의 장인님을, 하고 눈에서 불이 퍽 나서 그 아래 밭 있는 넝알로 그대로 떠밀어 굴려버렸다.
paragraphs.en: My father-in-law got even angrier and, right there, struck my shoulder with the pole. My mind went dizzy. When I raised my head again, my whole body was filled with fury. You wretched father-in-law, I thought, and sparks flew from my eyes, and I shoved him so that he rolled down into the gully where the field was below.

paragraphs.orig: "부려만 먹구 왜 성례 안하지유!"
paragraphs.en: "You just work me, why won't you hold the wedding!"

paragraphs.orig: 나는 이렇게 호령했다. 허지만 장인님이 선뜻 오냐 낼이라두 성례시켜 주마, 했으면 나도 성가신 걸 그만두었을지 모른다. 나야 이러면 때린 건 아니니까 나중에 장인 쳤다는 누명도 안 들을 터이고 얼마든지 해도 좋다.
paragraphs.en: I shouted like that. But if my father-in-law had readily said, all right, I'll hold the wedding tomorrow if you like, I might have stopped the bother. After all, it wasn't hitting, so later nobody would call me the man who hit his father-in-law, and I was free to do as much as I wished.

paragraphs.orig: 한번은 장인님이 헐떡헐떡 기어서 올라오더니 내 바짓가랭이를 요렇게 노리고서 단박 움켜잡고 매달렸다. 악, 소리를 치고 나는 그만 세상이 다 팽그르 도는 것이,
paragraphs.en: Once my father-in-law came panting up on all fours, aimed at the leg of my trousers like this, and immediately seized it and hung on. I cried out and the whole world seemed to spin,

paragraphs.orig: "빙장님! 빙장님! 빙장님!"
paragraphs.en: "Honoured Father-in-law! Honoured Father-in-law! Honoured Father-in-law!"

paragraphs.orig: "이자식! 잡아먹어라, 잡아먹어!"
paragraphs.en: "You rascal! Eat me, eat me up!"

paragraphs.orig: "아! 아! 할아버지! 살려줍쇼, 할아버지!"하고 두팔을 허둥지둥 내절 적에는 이마에 진땀이 쭉 내솟고 인젠 참으로 죽나보다 했다. 그래두 장인님은 놓질 않더니 내가 기어이 땅바닥에 쓰러져서 거진 까무러치게 되니까 놓는다. 더럽다, 더럽다. 이게 장인님인가? 나는 한참을 못 일어나고 쩔쩔맸다. 그러나 얼굴을 드니(눈엔 참 아무것도 보이지 않았다)사지가 부르르 떨리면서 나도 엉금엉금 기어가 장인님의 바짓가랭이를 꽉 움키고 잡아나꿨다.
paragraphs.en: "Ah! Ah! Grandfather! Spare me, Grandfather!" I cried, flailing both arms in a panic, with cold sweat gushing on my forehead, and thought that now I really would die. Even so my father-in-law didn't let go, and only when I finally collapsed on the ground, nearly fainting, did he release me. Dirty, dirty. Is this a father-in-law? For a good while I couldn't get up and flailed about. But when I raised my face (my eyes truly saw nothing), my limbs trembled and shook, and I too crawled on all fours to my father-in-law, clamped hold of his trouser leg, and yanked it.

paragraphs.orig: 내가 머리가 터지도록 매를 얻어맞은 것이 이 때문이다. 그러나 여기가 또한 우리 장인님이 유달리 착한 곳이다.
paragraphs.en: This is why I was beaten until my head split. But this is also where my father-in-law is unusually kind.

paragraphs.orig: 여느 사람이면 사경을 주어서라도 당장 내어쫓았지, 터진 머리를 볼솜으로 손수 지져 주고, 호주머니에 희연 한 봉을 넣어 주고 그리고,
paragraphs.en: Any other man would have driven me out on the spot, even if he had to pay my wages, but who else would himself dab my split head with cotton wool, put a packet of cheap tobacco in my pocket, and then,

paragraphs.orig: "올 갈엔 꼭 성례를 시켜 주마. 암만 말구 가서 뒷골의 콩밭이나얼른 갈아라." 하고 등을 뚜덕여 줄 사람이 누구냐. 나는 장인님이 너무나 고마워서 어느덧 눈물까지 났다.
paragraphs.en: "This autumn I'll surely hold the wedding. Don't worry, go and quickly plough the bean field in the back valley," and pat me on the back? I was so grateful to my father-in-law that before I knew it I was even in tears.

paragraphs.orig: 점순이를 남기고 인젠 내쫓기려니 하다 뜻밖의 말을 듣고,
paragraphs.en: I had thought that now I would be driven out, leaving Jeom-sun behind, and unexpectedly heard those words,

paragraphs.orig: "빙장님! 인제 다시는 안그러겠어유!"
paragraphs.en: "Honoured Father-in-law! I'll never do that again!"

paragraphs.orig: 이렇게 맹세를 하며 부랴부랴 지게를 지고 일터로 갔다. 그러나 이때는 그걸 모르고 장인님을 원수로만 여겨서 잔뜩 잡아당겼다.
paragraphs.en: I swore like this and hurriedly shouldered my A-frame and went to the work-site. But at that moment I didn't know that and regarded my father-in-law only as an enemy and pulled hard.

paragraphs.orig: "아! 아! 이놈아! 놔라, 놔."
paragraphs.en: "Ah! Ah! You rascal! Let go, let go."

paragraphs.orig: 장인님은 헷손질을 하며 솔개미에 챈 닭의 소리를 연해 질렀다. 놓긴 왜, 이왕이면 호되게 혼을 내주리라 생각하고 짖궂이 더 댕겼다. 마는 장인님이 땅에 쓰러져서 눈에 눈물이 피잉 도는 것을 알고 좀 겁도 났다.
paragraphs.en: My father-in-law, waving his arms wildly, kept screaming like a hen snatched by a kite. Let go? Why? Since I'm at it I'll give him a thorough lesson, I thought, and stubbornly pulled harder. But when I saw my father-in-law fallen on the ground with tears starting in his eyes, I got a bit frightened.

paragraphs.orig: "할아버지! 놔라, 놔, 놔, 놔, 놔라."
paragraphs.en: "Grandfather! Let go, let go, go, go, go!"

paragraphs.orig: 그래도 안되니까,
paragraphs.en: Even so it was no use, so he called,

paragraphs.orig: "애 점순아! 점순아!"
paragraphs.en: "Hey, Jeom-sun! Jeom-sun!"

paragraphs.orig: 이 악장에 안에 있었던 장모님과 점순이가 헐레벌떡하고 단숨에 뛰어 나왔다. 나의 생각에 장모님은 제 남편이니까 역성을 할는지도 모른다. 그러나 점순이는 내 편을 들어서 속으로 고수해 하겠지---. 대체 이게 웬 속인지(지금까지도 난 영문을 모른다) 아버질 혼내 주기는 제가 내래 놓고 이제 와서는 달겨들며,
paragraphs.en: At this shout my mother-in-law and Jeom-sun, who had been inside, came running out all in a rush. I thought my mother-in-law might take her husband's side, since he's her husband. But Jeom-sun would take my side, and be secretly pleased---. What on earth was in her heart (even now I don't know the reason), she had told me to teach her father a lesson, and now she flew at me and,

paragraphs.orig: "에그머니! 이 망할 게 아버지 죽이네!"
paragraphs.en: "Oh dear! This wretch is killing Father!"

paragraphs.orig: 하고, 귀를 뒤로 잡아댕기며 마냥 우는 것이 아니냐. 그만 여기에 기운이 탁 꺾이어 나는 얼빠진 등신이 되고 말았다. 장모님도 덤벼들어 한쪽 귀마저 뒤로 잡아채면서 또 우는 것이다.
paragraphs.en: she cried, pulling my ear backward, weeping and weeping. At that all my strength snapped, and I became a dazed fool. My mother-in-law too rushed in and yanked my other ear backward, and wept as well.

paragraphs.orig: 이렇게 꼼짝도 못하게 해놓고 장인님은 지게막대기를 들어서 사뭇 내려조졌다. 그러나 나는 구태여 피하려지도 않고 암만해도 그 속 알 수 없는 점순이의 얼굴만 멀거니 들여다보았다.
paragraphs.en: With me unable to move like this, my father-in-law lifted the A-frame pole and thrashed me with it without restraint. But I didn't even try to dodge, and only stared blankly at Jeom-sun's face, whose heart I could not make out.

paragraphs.orig: "이자식! 장인 입에서 할아버지 소리가 나오도록 해?"
paragraphs.en: "You rascal! Making your own father-in-law call you 'Grandfather'?"

review.notes: Full story to the last line, right work, PD (Kim Yu-jeong d. 1937); 1935 date is well-established. The original summary skipped and misordered events (headman scene, next-morning fight, Jeom-sun's ear-pulling); rewritten against the text in both languages. Author/context sections added 2026-10-08 and fact-checked by an independent reviewer (batch 1). Translation (2026-11-03) reviewed by an independent content-review agent: Read all 125 paragraphs. Fixes: 16 (대가릴 까놀자식 = skull-splitting threat, not 'shaved-head'), 17 (the rival tenant BRIBES the steward with money and wine; translation had it reversed), 18, 21 (건숭 = for show; ankle-sprain subject clarified), 42 (밤낮 일만 하다 말 텐가), 48 (심판 = what was going on), 74, 84 (fourth son-in-law 'should have come'), 87, 93 (병신 = dolt, not cripple), 114, 124. Register: 장인님 = 'father-in-law' throughout; 빙장님/빙모님 now 'Honoured Father-in-law/Mother-in-law' (paras 54, 55, 69, 106, 113), and the snake proverb in 54 is fixed (뱀두 뱀이래야 좋으냐 = does even a snake like being called a snake). The idiom 뿔 떨어지면 구워 먹지 does not occur in this text (it is in mullebanga). Remaining doubts: para 34 '새고 개 맞은 봉우리' is obscure and now rendered 'the peak across the pass' (previous 'struck by lightning' was unsupported); para 10 냇병 ('river sickness') is a guess at an unclear word; dialect lines 84-85 are standard prose and read fine. Section headings (2026-11-04) added at scene breaks and source ornament breaks; titles checked against the story by the orchestrating reviewer; text unchanged (pack check).
